en.headline: Youth membership in uniformed groups falls 8% over five years
en.dek: Home and Youth Affairs Bureau figures show total membership across 11 subsidised groups dropped from 117,671 to 108,551 between 2020-21 and 2024-25, linked to low birth rates.
body: Youth membership in Hong Kong’s 11 government-subsidised uniformed groups has declined by 8 per cent over the past five years, according to figures from the Home and Youth Affairs Bureau reported on Monday.

Total membership fell from 117,671 in the 2020-21 academic year to 108,551 in 2024-25. Over the past decade the drop has been nearly 18 per cent from 131,870 in 2013-14. The groups received HK$86 million in recurrent subsidies in 2024-25.

The Hong Kong Adventure Corps recorded the largest decline, falling 30 per cent from 4,882 to 3,403 members. The Hong Kong Road Safety Patrol saw a drop of more than 22 per cent. Membership also fell at the Scout Association of Hong Kong, the Guides Association and the Boys’ Brigade.

Six groups recorded growth, including the Association of Hong Kong Flag-guards and the Hong Kong Red Cross Youth. Lawmakers have called for key performance indicators to ensure prudent use of public funds, while some organisations expressed concern that linking funding to membership numbers could hinder development.

zh.headline: 制服團體青年會員五年跌8% 出生率低為主因
zh.dek: 民政及青年事務局數字顯示，11個受資助制服團體會員由2020-21年11.7萬人降至2024-25年10.8萬人，十年間跌近18%。
body: 香港11個獲政府資助的青年制服團體會員人數過去五年下跌約8%，民政及青年事務局數字顯示，2020-21學年共有117,671名會員，至2024-25學年降至108,551人。
過去十年會員數目由2013-14年的131,870人下跌近18%。該等團體於2024-25學年共獲8,600萬元經常資助。
香港青少年軍跌幅最大，由4,882人減至3,403人，跌約30%；香港交通安全隊跌逾22%。童軍總會、女童軍總會及基督少年軍會員亦見減少。
六個團體錄得增長，包括香港升旗隊總會及香港紅十字會青年團。有立法會議員建議引入關鍵績效指標以確保公帑運用得宜，部分組織則擔心將資助與會員人數掛鈎或影響發展。
